A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Distilled Circuits and retain identifiable methods, case studies, and figures. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices support reliable comparison despite substantial expansion and reorganization.

before.justification: Sections 3–4 and Appendices E–F report original circuit analyses, component ablations, noise-injection experiments, and teacher–student alignment measurements.

after.justification: V2 retains original empirical analyses and adds Llama/Minitron experiments, causal role validation, linear probes, robustness quantification, and sensitivity studies.

M1.justification: The alignment metric retains its three-step structure and final aggregation, but v2 specifies average absolute cosine similarity for MLP principal components, whereas v1 specifies average cosine similarity. This is a limited revision to the reported scoring rule. Many-to-one matching also resolves v1's inconsistent description of nearest-neighbor matching as one-to-one; that wording alone does not establish a different implemented matcher.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate numeral sequence completion, word sequence completion, indirect object identification, and SimpleQA using the same data sources. V2 extends model participation and diagnostic analyses within this coverage. The newly documented checkpoint training corpora do not establish additional training datasets used by this work.

E2.justification: Appendix M/Table 5 adds evaluated alternatives to the default metric configuration: Hungarian and soft top-k matching, together with L1 and L2 influence normalization. These are limited internal comparison variants. CKA and SVCCA remain discussed alternatives without reported experimental comparisons in either version.

E3.justification: The main cross-task evaluation changes from 100 examples per task to 384 for sequence completion, 500 for IOI, and 200 for SimpleQA. V2 adds the Llama-3.1-8B/Minitron-4B model configuration and held-out probe evaluations with sampling and permutation controls. It also revises the reported logit-difference definition. These substantially expand and revise evaluation settings without establishing that every retained experiment was rerun.

E4.justification: V2 adds targeted activation-patching and linear-probe tests of component roles, circuit completeness and faithfulness checks, larger-model ablation analyses, and compression–robustness quantification. Appendices M–N additionally test sensitivity to normalization, matching, and extraction thresholds. These address causal attribution and methodological stability beyond v1's existing ablations and noise-injection analysis.

E5.justification: V1 reports five-seed standard-deviation error bars for the noise experiment. V2 retains that practice and adds 95% confidence intervals to cross-task metrics, bootstrap intervals for mean ablation-induced drops, and intervals for compression–robustness coefficients. Uncertainty reporting therefore becomes substantially broader; the PDFs do not indicate an increase in the noise experiment's seed count.

E6.justification: V1 Table 2 becomes v2 Table 3 with revised results and samples: GPT numeral alignment, for example, changes from 0.9356 to 0.9452. Llama results and BERT word-completion results are added, while the GPT SimpleQA row is removed. New probe, robustness, and sensitivity results substantially expand the evidence. Table 1 and the original figure graphics are retained. Changed aggregate scores should not be interpreted as same-setting performance gains.

T1.justification: Equation 3 replaces the difference of probability log-odds with the correct softmax logit difference, log(p_correct/p_incorrect), correcting the mathematical definition. V2 also revises the stated MLP similarity definition and adds limited computational-complexity reasoning. The final alignment aggregation remains equivalent, and no substantial theorem or proof framework is introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion extend the claimed applicability to larger Llama/Minitron models. The conclusion explicitly qualifies detailed circuit decompositions as task- and model-specific while proposing broader transfer of compression, reliance, and omission trends. The central contributions—mechanistic analysis of distillation and the alignment metric—remain unchanged.

C2.justification: V2 interprets T-L1-H5 primarily as encoding the previous numeral rather than detecting repetition. It removes the failed-GPT-SimpleQA fallback-circuit interpretation and adds explanations for Llama's higher alignment, including the metric's built-in dependence on influence agreement. Sections 4.3 and 5.1 substantially expand practical recommendations, task-conditioned applicability, scalability constraints, and limitations concerning model diversity and distillation regimes.

D1.justification: New Appendix A documents released checkpoints, training corpora, distillation objectives, and Minitron's pruning/training provenance. Appendix J supplies probe implementation details, including Adam, learning rate 0.001, 20 epochs, and an 80/20 split. V2 also updates model-size documentation and specifies sensitivity configurations. These substantially improve technical disclosure; the supplied code-repository access information remains unchanged.

R1.justification: V2 adds references supporting Llama/Minitron, training-data provenance, successor-head validation, and interpretability agents, while removing the Nainani reference associated with the deleted fallback-circuit discussion. The main knowledge-distillation and mechanistic-interpretability positioning is retained. Citation-style and bibliographic updates do not constitute substantive positioning changes.

P1.justification: V2 substantially expands and rewrites methodological explanations, the cross-task discussion, and limitations. It introduces dedicated task descriptions and practical-use guidance, separates robustness into its own subsection, and reorganizes the appendices while retaining their original case studies. These are substantial narrative and structural changes beyond the added experiments.

P2.justification: V2 adopts a different journal template and extensively reflows figures and tables. It restructures the cross-task table to separate model pairs and display confidence intervals, adds three tables and five figures, and relocates retained graphics. A new caption error labels the retained GPT IOI histograms in Figure 15 as BERT.

improvement.justification: V1 largely inferred component roles from attention and representation patterns and lacked sensitivity checks for key metric and extraction choices. V2 adds targeted causal/probe validation, normalization and matching comparisons, threshold sweeps, larger-model replication, and broader uncertainty reporting. Together with the corrected logit definition and implementation disclosures, these substantially strengthen evidential support and reproducibility. Presentation defects, including Figure 15's incorrect model label, do not outweigh these gains.
